figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption: Fig. 1. Workﬂow of article identiﬁcation and curation for experimentally veriﬁed BGCs. NT refers to the nucleotide records in GenBank.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. Overlaps between curated articles and nucleotide records in this study versus those in the ClusterMine360 database (CM360). The ﬁrst row (A and B) represents the
overlaps at the article level, while the second row (C and D) represents the overlaps at the nucleotide entry level. ‘‘Initial Set” (in A and C) includes the 275 articles and
associated nucleotide records obtained by semi-automated selection. The ‘‘Final curation” set (in B and D) includes the conﬁrmed article-nucleotide pairs from 217 articles,
which are annotated with at least one compound.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Global network view of conﬁrmed article-compound relationships. A. An overview of the network between the articles and compounds. The network contains 393
article compound pairs between 217 articles (purple nodes) and 197 compounds (green nodes). B. The node degree distributions of the article nodes and compound nodes
both follow the power-law distributions. C. The sub-network (a connected component) containing T-2 Toxin. D. The sub-network containing aﬂatoxins.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4. The 15 most frequently studied compounds (A), and the most frequently studied fungal genera (B) and classes (C) associated with compounds in the curated set of
experimentally veriﬁed natural product gene clusters. For (A), Closely related compounds are manually merged into compound families. # Articles: number of unique articles
covering one or more compounds in each family. # Species: number of unique species origins of the nucleotides associated with these articles.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 5. Hierarchical clustering of 685 fungal metabolites in ChEBI and 197 compounds in our catalog (marked yellow). (For interpretation of the references to colour in this
ﬁgure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 6. Phylogenetic tree constructed using the KS domains of the PKS core enzymes identiﬁed by homology in sequenced fungal genomes from GenBank. Characterized PKSs
from this study are highlighted with yellow diamonds. The numerical values associated with the internal nodes are estimated reliability values for the splits generated by the
Shimodaira–Hasegawa test.
